title: Projective internal Hom is exact on the one-object ring site
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, and regard $A$-modules as sheaves on the category with one object and only its identity, with bottom topology and constant ring $A$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $M$ be such a sheaf whose value $M(*)$ is projective over $A$, meaning that linear maps from it lift through every surjective linear map. For every short exact sequence $0\to N_1\xrightarrow{f}N_2\xrightarrow{g}N_3\to0$, the induced sequence $0\to\mathcal Hom_A(M,N_1)\xrightarrow{f_*}\mathcal Hom_A(M,N_2)\xrightarrow{g_*}\mathcal Hom_A(M,N_3)\to0$ of the shared internal Hom sheaves [def-pur-sheaf-hom] is short exact. No finite-generation hypothesis is imposed on $M(*)$.

source.place: Definition 05CE (definition-projective), projective Hom exactness; more-algebra.tex Lemma 0A6A (lemma-base-change-RHom), projective-source computation

proof.text: Evaluation at the unique object and the constant presheaf construction are inverse up to their componentwise identity maps. The only restriction maps are identities and the bottom topology requires no extra condition. These give an additive equivalence with A-modules, preserving and reflecting short exact sequences. The slice at the unique object also has exactly one object up to unique isomorphism. Evaluation of the shared internal Hom identifies it with linear Hom_A(M(*),N(*)); its two maps become postcomposition by f(*) and g(*).

Postcomposition by the injection f is injective. A map t:M(*)→N_2(*) killed by g has image in ker(g)=im(f), and uniquely factors through f because f is injective; the resulting factor is A-linear. Projectivity lifts every map M(*)→N_3(*) through the surjection g. Thus the evaluated Hom sequence is short exact. Its composite is zero because f followed by g is zero. Reflect this sequence through evaluation. The proof includes the zero ring, zero source and infinite-rank projectives.
